newsitem.title: USA: Nasdaq hit, techs soften on earnings, margin fears.
newsitem.headline: Nasdaq hit, techs soften on earnings, margin fears.

text.p: Nasdaq shares ended the week on a down note after fears about earnings and profit margins muffled some technology stocks, traders said.

The Nasdaq Composite Index dropped 12.85 points or 0.95 percent to close unofficially at 1340.73. Declining issues beat advancing issues 2,171 to 2,022 on volume of 574.5 million. Nasdaq share have lost ground in only three of the previous 10 sessions.
"The broader market was soft all day ahead of next week's (Federal Reserve policy) meeting. But the techs got hit by some fears of bad earnings," one trader said.

Hewlett-Packard Co, a component of the Dow Industrials which trades on New York Stock Exchange, set the tone for trading in technology shares, traders said. Shares of Hewlett-Packard dropped 11 percent after the company's second quarter fell short of analysts' estimates.

Netscape Communications Corp sank 5-5/16 to 29-1/4 after the Internet access software maker warned of slower revenue and earnings growth. PairGain Technologies Inc , the most heavily-traded Nasdaq issue, fell 3-7/8 to 17-1/4 after a SoundView Financial Group analyst raised concerns about pricing pressures.
